topics.name: Basic economic ideas and resource allocation

questions.q: A positive statement is one that…
questions.why: Normative statements contain opinions about what ought to be.

questions.q: The ceteris paribus assumption means…
questions.why: It isolates the effect of one variable.

questions.q: In a mixed economy, resources are allocated by…
o: both the market and the state
questions.why: Most economies combine private markets with public provision.

long.q: Use a production possibility curve to explain the meaning of opportunity cost.
scheme: B1: opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up
B1: a PPC shows the combinations of two goods that can be made with all resources fully used
B1: moving along the curve, making more of one good means making less of the other: that amount is the opportunity cost

topics.name: The price system and the microeconomy

questions.q: Income elasticity of demand is negative. The good is…
questions.why: Demand for inferior goods falls as income rises.

questions.q: Cross elasticity of demand between two goods is positive. They are…
questions.why: A rise in one's price raises demand for the other.

questions.q: Consumer surplus is…
o: the difference between what consumers are willing to pay and what they pay
questions.why: It is the area below the demand curve and above the price.

questions.q: If demand is price inelastic, a price rise will…
questions.why: Quantity falls proportionally less than price rises.

long.q: When the price of a good rises from $10 to $12, the quantity demanded falls from 500 to 450 units. Calculate the price elasticity of demand and explain what happens to total revenue.
scheme: M1: % change in quantity = −10%; % change in price = +20%
B1: demand is price inelastic
B1: total revenue rises, from $5000 to $5400

questions.q: An indirect tax on a good with inelastic demand falls mainly on…
questions.why: Producers can pass most of the tax on as higher prices.

questions.q: A negative externality of production leads a free market to…
questions.why: Firms ignore external costs, so marginal social cost exceeds private cost.

questions.q: A public good is…
questions.why: These features create the free-rider problem.

long.q: Explain why a maximum price set below the equilibrium price may lead to a shortage and a black market.
scheme: B1: at the lower price quantity demanded rises
B1: and quantity supplied falls
B1: so there is excess demand (a shortage)
B1: some buyers will pay more than the legal price, so goods are sold illegally above it

questions.q: Aggregate demand is…
questions.why: Consumption, investment, government spending and net exports.

questions.q: Cost-push inflation is caused by…
o: rising costs of production, such as wages or oil
questions.why: Higher costs shift short-run aggregate supply left.

questions.q: Which is counted as unemployed?
o: Someone able and willing to work and actively seeking work
questions.why: The ILO definition requires being without work, available and looking.

long.q: Distinguish between demand-pull and cost-push inflation.
scheme: B1: demand-pull: aggregate demand rises faster than aggregate supply / the economy's capacity
B1: an example cause: rising consumer spending, lower interest rates, more government spending
B1: cost-push: rising costs of production push up the price level (AS shifts left)
B1: an example cause: higher wages, oil or import prices, a weaker exchange rate

questions.q: Expansionary fiscal policy involves…
o: raising government spending or cutting taxes
questions.why: It boosts aggregate demand.

questions.q: Supply-side policies aim to…
o: increase the productive capacity of the economy
questions.why: Examples: education, training, deregulation, infrastructure.

long.q: Explain how a rise in the central bank's rate of interest might reduce inflation.
scheme: B1: borrowing becomes more expensive and saving more rewarding
B1: so consumption and investment fall
B1: aggregate demand falls (also via a stronger exchange rate cutting net exports)
B1: so demand-pull pressure on the price level eases

questions.q: Comparative advantage means a country should specialise where it has…
questions.why: Trade can benefit both countries even if one is better at everything.

questions.q: The Marshall–Lerner condition states a depreciation improves the current account if…
questions.why: Sum of export and import price elasticities (absolute values) must exceed 1.

long.q: A worker in Country A can make 10 units of wheat or 5 units of cloth. A worker in Country B can make 6 units of wheat or 6 units of cloth. Explain which country has a comparative advantage in each good.
scheme: M1: opportunity cost of 1 cloth: A gives up 2 wheat, B gives up 1 wheat
M1: opportunity cost of 1 wheat: A gives up 0.5 cloth, B gives up 1 cloth
B1: A has the comparative advantage in wheat
B1: B has the comparative advantage in cloth, so each should specialise and trade

topics.name: The price system and the microeconomy (A Level)

questions.q: A firm maximises profit where…
questions.why: Producing one more unit would add more to cost than to revenue beyond that point.

questions.q: In perfect competition in the long run, firms earn…
questions.why: Free entry and exit remove supernormal profit.

questions.q: A natural monopoly arises because of…
o: economies of scale so large that one firm has the lowest cost
questions.why: Examples include water and electricity grids.

questions.q: The Gini coefficient measures…
questions.why: 0 means perfect equality; 1 means maximum inequality.

questions.q: Government failure occurs when…
o: intervention leads to a less efficient allocation of resources
questions.why: Causes include poor information and unintended consequences.

questions.q: The multiplier is larger when the marginal propensity to consume is…
questions.why: In a closed economy without government, k = 1/(1 − MPC).

questions.q: The natural rate of unemployment is associated with…
questions.why: It exists when the labour market is in equilibrium.

questions.q: Quantitative easing means the central bank…
o: buys financial assets to increase the money supply
questions.why: It aims to lower long-term interest rates and boost spending.

questions.q: Which measure of development adjusts income for differences in prices between countries?
questions.why: PPP compares how much a unit of income buys in each country.
